main_text.p: shew not thy ialse vnkind[?], And suffer not his benefits Tosl[?] p out of thy minde,&c.

HVNGARICA lingua audio impressum esse novum Testamentum, sed fere inutiliter ]? imo & vetus & novum Testamentum hac lingua elegantibus typis descripta extant Herbor-nae,anno M DC. VII. interprete pio & erudito viro, Alberto Molnar. Id vero non inutiliter: sed excellenti bono orthodoxarum ecclesiarum in regno Hungariae,&c.

IACOBITAE in linguâ Græcâ similibus characteribus utuntur.] Vt videre est apud Theseum[?] Ambrosium in Introductione linguarum, ex alphabeto eorum, quod habetur pag. 191. quem adi. Alioquin gens sunt Syrorum, qui perpetuò per o efferunt vocalem, quem Syri Odom vocant, quæ respondet Hebraeorum kamerz.

ICHTYOPHAGI Arabice ferè & Persice loquuntur.] Sunt enim maximam partè Saraceni, tum albo, tum nigro colore tincti: & Ichtyophagi dicti, quod supra petras, Solis feruore feruentes, assant pisces, & hoc alimento solo vi&itant; quorum regio quæ amplissima, & perpaucos habet portus maritimos, hodie appellatur regnum Vlcinde, inter Persidem & Indiam situm. Ad ortu enim re-gno Cambajâ, ad occasu Perside terminatur.

page.notes: Printer's bracket marks "]" after "inutiliter" and "utuntur." are typographic signs (possibly a reference or Hebrew-style sign) and are only approximated. "Tosl" in the first verse lines is doubtful; the line "shew not thy ialse vnkind" is partly obscured. "vnkind" is doubtful. "Theseum" is doubtful (possibly Thesaurum). "II6" in the header is read as 116. Hebrew kamerz is copied as printed and may be a different spelling. The Greek and Hebrew terms are rendered in Latin letters only where the print is in Latin letters; no Greek or Hebrew script is visible.
